result.title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
result.summary: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察自监督单目深度网络所预测逐像素不确定度的校准问题（尺度与形状），并提出 MonoCal：用立体图像对估计一个常数来校正尺度，并通过让不确定度预测两个自监督网络深度不一致的位置来重训形状，无需真值深度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“无标签、以双网络分歧作为不确定度监督”的思路可供核查是否能迁移到 LVR 的证据可信度估计与停止/再看的决策；但该文属稠密深度预测，未涉及推理状态，联系较远。
